Men's Basketball |url=https://auburntigers.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/johni-broome/18101 |access-date=February 18, 2023 |website=Auburn University Athletics |language=en}} born July 19, 2002) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Morehead State Eagles men's basketball|Morehead State Eagles]] and [[Auburn Tigers men's basketball|Auburn Tigers]]. ==High school career== Broome attended [[Plant City High School]] in [[Plant City, Florida]], and grew about six inches (15 cm) in two years. He transferred to [[Tampa Catholic High School]] in [[Tampa, Florida]].{{cite web |last1=Putnam |first1=Bob |title=Tampa Catholic's Johni Broome finds his calling in the gym, not the gridiron |url=https://www.tampabay.com/sports/high-schools/2020/03/03/tampa-catholics-johni-broome-finds-his-calling-in-the-gym-not-the-gridiron/ |website=[[Tampa Bay Times]] |access-date=March 17, 2021 |date=March 3, 2020}} As a senior, Broome averaged 19.6 points, 10.9 rebounds, and 2.2 blocks per game, and was named [[Hillsborough County, Florida|Hillsborough County]] Player of the Year.{{cite web |last1=Burke Sr. |first1=Reginald |title=2019-20 Tampa Bay Boys Baseball All-Hillsborough County POY, First & Second Team |url=http://bayareahoops.com/archives/9540 |website=Bay Area throws |access-date=March 17, 2021 |date=April 27, 2020}} He committed to playing college basketball for [[Morehead State Eagles men's basketball|Morehead State]] over offers from [[Florida Atlantic Owls men's basketball|Florida Atlantic]], [[Georgia Southern Eagles men's basketball|Georgia Southern]], [[Jacksonville Dolphins men's basketball|Jacksonville]], and [[Bryant Bulldogs men's basketball|Bryant]].{{cite web |last1=Schabert |first1=Matt |title=Men's Basketball Inks 6-10 Rising Star Johni Broome From the Sunshine State |url=https://msueagles.com/news/2019/12/4/mens-basketball-inks-6-10-rising-star-johni-broome.aspx |website=Morehead State University Athletics |access-date=March 17, 2021 |date=December 4, 2019}} ==College career== Broome immediately assumed an important role at Morehead State after Tyzhun Claude suffered a torn [[anterior cruciate ligament]] during practice before the season.{{cite web |last1=Sullivan |first1=Josh |title='Wow, we've really got something here.' Freshman big man Broome has Morehead rising. |url=https://www.kentucky.com/sports/college/article249157975.html |website=[[Lexington Herald-Leader]] |access-date=March 17, 2021 |date=February 12, 2021}} At the conclusion of the regular season, he was named [[Ohio Valley Conference]] (OVC) Player of the Year and earned First Team All-OVC honors.{{cite web |last1=Bennett |first1=Brian |title=Meet Morehead State, a team as hot as any heading into the NCAA Tournament |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/2437872/2021/03/10/morehead-state-2021-ncaa-tournament-johni-broome/ |website=[[The Athletic]] |access-date=March 17, 2021 |date=March 10, 2021}} He was a nine-time OVC Freshman of the Week, breaking the program record previously held by [[Kenneth Faried]], who earned the accolade eight times.{{cite web |last1=Schabert |first1=Matt |last2=Vallejo |first2=Matteo |title=Broome Breaks Another Record With Ninth OVC Freshman of the Week Honor |url=https://msueagles.com/news/2021/3/1/mens-basketball-broome-breaks-another-record-with-ninth-ovc-freshman-of-the-week-honor.aspx |website=Morehead State University Athletics |access-date=March 17, 2021 |date=March 1, 2021}} On March 6, 2021, Broome posted 27 points and 12 rebounds in an 86–71 win over top-seeded [[Belmont Bruins men's basketball|Belmont]] at the [[2021 Ohio Valley Conference men's basketball tournament|OVC tournament]] final. He was named tournament MVP.{{cite web |last1=Patton |first1=Kevin |title=Morehead State wins Ohio Valley Conference tournament championship, beats Belmont 86-71 |url=https://www.courierpress.com/story/sports/2021/03/06/morehead-state-rides-johni-broome-into-ncaa-ovc-tournament-title/4592521001/ |website=[[Evansville Courier & Press]] |access-date=March 17, 2021 |date=March 6, 2021}} Broome averaged 13.8 points, nine rebounds, and 1.9 blocks per game as a freshman.{{cite web |last1=Welser |first1=Joel |title=#120 MOREHEAD STATE MEN'S BASKETBALL 2021-2022 PREVIEW |url=https://www.collegesportsmadness.com/article/19597 |website=College Sports Madness |access-date=October 2, 2021 |date=July 13, 2021}} He averaged 16.8 points, 10.5 rebounds, and 3.9 blocks per game as a sophomore. As a sophomore, Broome was again named to the First Team All-OVC, as well as Defensive Player of the Year.{{cite press release|url=http://ovcsports.com/news/2022/2/28/murray-states-williams-and-mcmahon-morehead-states-broome-and-apsus-hutchins-everett-earn-2021-22-ovc-mens-basketball-top-honors.aspx|title=Murray State's Williams and McMahon, Morehead State's Broome and APSU's Hutchins-Everett Earn 1921-22 OVC Men's Basketball Top Honors|publisher=[[Ohio Valley Conference]] |date=March 1, 2022 |accessdate=March 1, 2022}} On April 4, 2022, Broome entered the [[NCAA transfer portal|transfer portal]].{{cite web | url=https://www.on3.com/teams/kentucky-wildcats/news/morehead-state-star-johni-broome-puts-name-transfer-portal/ | title=Morehead State star Johni Broome puts name in transfer ptal |work=[[ESPN]]| date=April 4, 2022 |accessdate=February 23, 2023}} On April 30, 2022, Broome announced that he would be transferring to [[Auburn Tigers men's basketball|Auburn]] over [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Florida]].{{Cite web |last=Borzello |first=Jeff |date=April 30, 2022 |title=ESPN top 10 transfer Broome commits to Auburn |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/33833544/johni-broome-espn-top-10-transfers-chooses-join-auburn-men-basketball-program |access-date=February 23, 2022 |website=[[ESPN]]}} In the 2024–25 season, Broome helped Auburn secure a top seed in the [[2025 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA Division I tournament]] by leading the Tigers in points, rebounds, assists, and blocks. He was named [[The Sporting News Men's College Basketball Player of the Year|''The Sporting News'' Men's College Basketball Player of the Year]].{{cite news |last1=Trocchi |first1=Bill |title=Sporting News 2024-25 College Basketball Player of the Year: Johni Broome's final year his best yet |url=https://www.sportingnews.com/us/ncaa-basketball/auburn/news/sporting-news-college-basketball-player-year-johni-broome/c27834b8c40738af562d278c |access-date=14 May 2025 |work=[[The Sporting News]] |date=13 March 2025 |language=en-us}} In his final season at Auburn, Broome scored 669 points and had 389 rebounds which ranks 7th and 1st, respectively, for [[Auburn Tigers men's basketball statistical leaders]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/stats/_/id/4433569/type/mens-college-basketball|publisher=ESPN|title=Johni Broome NCAA Stats}} He scored 1,245 points over his final two seasons, which broke the two-year scoring record previously held by [[KT Harrell]] (1,196).{{cite web|url=https://auburntigers.com/staff/kt-harrell|publisher=Auburn Tigers Athletics|title=KT Harrell Staff Profile}} His total points rank 8th (1,712), career scoring average ranks 10th (16.5), career rebounding average ranks 6th (9.3), total rebounds rank 2nd (965) and total blocks rank 3rd all time (232).{{cite web|url=https://auburntigers.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/player/johni-broome|title=Johni Broome Auburn Tigers Profile}} ==Professional career== ===Philadelphia 76ers (2025–2026)=== Broome was selected by the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] with the 35th pick in the [[2025 NBA Draft]].{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/45593263/rasheer-fleming-goes-suns-no-31-2025-nba-draft-resumes |title=76ers grab Broome, Suns land Fleming in Round 2 of NBA draft |date=June 26, 2025 |accessdate=July 1, 2025}} In his [[pre-season]] debut against the [[New York Knicks]] in [[Abu Dhabi]], Broome scored four points and had six rebounds.{{cite web |title=Johni Broome |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/_/id/4433569/johni-broome |website=ESPN |access-date=October 4, 2025}} On January 16, 2026, while playing for the [[Delaware Blue Coats]], Broome recorded 50 points and 17 rebounds in a 155–140 victory over the [[College Park Skyhawks]].{{Cite web|title=76ers Rookie Johni Broome Notches 50-Point Double-Double in G League|url=https://www.si.com/nba/draft/nba-rookies/76ers-rookie-johni-broome-notches-50-point-double-double-in-g-league-01kf6descry1|access-date=February 2, 2026|website=si.com|language=en}} On February 22, Broome was ruled out indefinitely after being diagnosed with a lateral [[meniscus tear]] in his right knee.{{Cite web|title=Sixers rookie Broome suffers lateral meniscus tear|url=https://www.nbcsportsphiladelphia.com/nba/philadelphia-76ers/johni-broome-meniscus-tear-sixers-injury-news/716992/?amp=1|access-date=February 28, 2026|website=nbcsportsphiladelphia.com|language=en}} On May 4, Broome made his [[NBA playoffs]] debut, where he played five minutes in game one against the [[2025–26 New York Knicks season|New York Knicks]], in that game, he tallied up just one rebound while going 0-1 from the field.{{cite web |title=76ers' Johni Broome: Makes garbage-time cameo |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/76ers-johni-broome-makes-garbage-time-cameo/ |website=[[CBS Sports]] |date=May 5, 2026 |access-date=June 14, 2026 }} On May 10, he played three minutes for the 76ers, scoring seven points and tallying one rebound and one assist. He went 3-for-5 from the [[field goal]] and 1-for-3 from the [[three point line]]. ===Los Angeles Clippers (2026–present)=== On July 28, 2026, Broome was traded to the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] to free up a roster spot for [[Kentavious Caldwell-Pope]].{{Cite web |date=2026-07-28 |title=Clippers' Johni Broome: Heading to LAC |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/clippers-johni-broome-heading-to-lac/ |access-date=2026-07-28 |website=CBS Sports |language=en}}{{Cite web |date=2026-07-28 |title=PHILADELPHIA
